title: Sequential Spinodal Decompositions and Ordering Reactions in an As-Quenched Cr<sub>39</sub>Co<sub>18</sub>Fe<sub>18</sub>Ni<sub>18</sub>Al<sub>7</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: As-quenched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 high-entropy alloy (nominally a single BCC solid-solution).
recollection.intervention: Isothermal ageing/annealing at intermediate temperatures (≈600–800 °C for hours to tens of hours) to trigger phase separation and ordering.
recollection.structure: A hierarchical microstructure produced by two sequential events: (1) spinodal compositional modulations that partition the alloy into Cr-rich and (Co,Fe,Ni,Al)-rich BCC regions; (2) within the (Co,Fe,Ni,Al)-rich regions, B2-ordered (Ni,Co)Al nanoprecipitates form, giving a mixture of BCC (A2) matrix + B2 precipitates with nanoscale periodicity (~5–15 nm).
recollection.mechanism: Early-stage continuous (spinodal) decomposition amplifies compositional fluctuations throughout the supersaturated BCC solid solution. As ageing proceeds, the Al- and Ni-enriched regions reach the stoichiometry for B2 ordering, so an A2→B2 transition occurs inside those regions, while Cr segregation continues, leading to a second, coarser spinodal wavelength. The sequential nature (spinodal, then ordering) is driven by differences in chemical driving forces and diffusivities of the constituent elements.
recollection.results: (Guessed) Hardness roughly doubles from ~2.5 GPa in the as-quenched state to ~5 GPa after 24 h at 700 °C; compressive yield strength increases from ~900 MPa to ~1.7 GPa while maintaining ≈8 % plastic strain. Atom-probe tomography shows ~40 % volume fraction of 3–5 nm B2 precipitates; small-angle X-ray scattering gives a primary spinodal wavelength of ~10 nm and a secondary coarser wavelength of ~40 nm after long ageing.

score.note: The annealing treatment is incorrect: the paper used 1100–1300 °C for 30–60 min followed by water quenching, not 600–800 °C ageing for many hours. The recollection correctly identifies a hierarchical BCC/B2 microstructure and Ni–Al enrichment associated with B2 ordering, but misses the reciprocal structure of BCC nanoparticles inside larger B2 particles and misstates some partitioning. The broad spinodal-decomposition-then-ordering mechanism is correct, although it is incorrectly framed as an isothermal-ageing process and includes unsupported wavelength/diffusivity details. The hardness, strength, strain, volume fraction, and wavelength values are largely fabricated and do not match the reported HRC values, particle sizes, or phase fraction.
